body_markdown:
[Press Release](https://www.elcompanies.com/en/news-and-media/newsroom) , Oct 28, 2026


Today, The Estée Lauder Companies released its[Fiscal 2026 Social Impact & Sustainability Report](https://media.elcompanies.com/files/e/estee-lauder-companies/global/our-impact/si-s26/sis-2026.pdf) . This annual report outlines the company’s progress against its social impact and sustainability goals, reflecting The Estée Lauder Companies’ continued focus on transparency and accountability while supporting long-term business resilience and innovation.


“For 80 years, our company has been built on more than exceptional beauty products. We have believed in the power of beauty to inspire confidence, create opportunities, and make a positive difference in people’s lives,” said **Stéphane de La Faverie** , President and Chief Executive Officer, The Estée Lauder Companies, and President, The Estée Lauder Companies Charitable Foundation. “From our longstanding commitment to advancing women and girls globally, and our mission to create a breast cancer-free world, to our efforts to protect the environment, social impact and sustainability have long been part of who we are.”


“Our focus is on translating sustainability insights into action, understanding what matters most to consumers, informing product development and innovation, strengthening transparency and claims, and helping our brands deliver experiences that build relevance and trust,” said **Nancy Mahon** , Chief Sustainability Officer, The Estée Lauder Companies.


Covering the period from July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026, the report details progress and ongoing work across the company’s brands, operations, and value chain, including against a slate of 2030 social impact and sustainability goals. Key areas include employee health and safety, employee experience, climate, sourcing, product formulation and packaging, water, waste, and social impact philanthropic activities supporting women and girls.


Key highlights from the FY26 SI&S Report include:


Sustainability


- **Continued progress on packaging sustainability1** : 67% of packaging designed to be recyclable, 21% post-consumer recycled material in packaging and 94% responsibly sourced forest-based fiber in paper packaging2.
- **Achieved GreenCircle certification across multiple brands:** Extending the visibility of the Company’s sustainability efforts directly to consumers at the point of purchase.
- **Launched a new 2030 goal to evaluate 100% of products with a life-cycle assessment and eco-design approach:** This work is designed to help the company better understand environmental impacts across product life cycles and inform future product innovation, sustainability strategies, and supply chain decisions.3, 4
- **Advanced progress toward climate goals:** Achieved a 44% reduction in absolute Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions from its fiscal 2018 baseline5 and a nearly 23% reduction in absolute Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions from its fiscal 2018 baseline6.
- **Maintained 100% renewable electricity across direct operations — for seventh consecutive year:** Continued to source renewable electricity for our direct operations through a combination of on-site generation, utility contracts, energy attribute certificates, and our virtual power purchase agreement7.
- **Exceeded the 2030 water withdrawal target:** Achieved a 55% reduction in absolute water withdrawal at direct manufacturing sites from its fiscal 2019 baseline8, exceeding the 2030 target of at least a 50% reduction.
- **Exceeded 2030 waste reduction target:** Achieved a 33% reduction in absolute waste from direct manufacturing and distribution sites from its fiscal 2023 baseline9, exceeding the 2030 target of at least a 15% reduction. Maintained zero industrial waste-to-landfill across our global manufacturing, distribution, and innovation sites.
- **Exceeded annual palm oil goal:** Sourced 97% of our palm-based ingredients through RSPO-certified sustainable physical supply chains10, exceeding our annual commitment of at least 95%.


Social Impact and People


- **Advanced social philanthropy projects supporting women and girls:** Over $16 million toward its 2030 commitment to contribute $50 million in social impact philanthropy projects supporting women’s and girls’ health, education, leadership and entrepreneurship11.
- **Continued the legacy and impact of The Estée Lauder Companies’ Breast Cancer Campaign:** Through the end of fiscal 2026, The Breast Cancer Campaign and The Estée Lauder Companies Charitable Foundation have funded more than $167 million for lifesaving research, education and medical services around the world, including more than $131 million for medical research through the Breast Cancer Research Foundation.
- **Strengthened safety culture worldwide and achieved employee safety goal:** Increased training, employee engagement, and safety improvement initiatives across our global operations, implemented more than 350 safety projects to enhance site safety, and achieved target Total Recordable Incident Rate12.
- **Enhanced employee volunteerism and giving program:** Continued to engage employees in giving and volunteerism opportunities, raising $2.5 million toward the 2030 commitment of $10 million to nonprofits13.
- **Strengthened philanthropic support for women and girls through corporate and brand-led initiatives:** Building on Mrs. Estée Lauder’s legacy, the company continued its philanthropy supporting women and girls through initiatives including *M·A·C VIVA GLAM’s* mission towards healthy futures for all; the *Estée Lauder Emerging Leaders Fund* , which expanded its Beautiful Forces grants supporting women-led community initiatives and has trained more than 600 emerging leaders from over 80 countries; and the company’s *BEAUTY&YOU Indi* a, India’s leading beauty entrepreneurship program that supports women entrepreneurs through its Visionary Women’s Award.


[Read more in the FY26 Social Impact and Sustainability Report](https://www.elcompanies.com/en/our-impact/social-impact-and-sustainability-report)
